minutes.headline: Personnel Committee voted to amend SAP vacation rules after a split over its role on grievances and layoffs.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a heated discussion of the committee's charge, with some members worried that recent SAP changes on grievances and layoffs weaken employee protections. The committee then worked through the SAP vacation section. It voted to drop a proposed May 1 carryover deadline, adopted revised wording on termination payout, vacation approval and advance vacation, and began paid holidays but tabled it. The next meeting was set for March 2.

public_comment.topic: A new committee member said she is uncomfortable voting on SAP language changes, including grievance and layoff, until the committee clarifies its role.
A member asked the committee to agree on the personnel committee's roles and responsibilities before voting on further recommendations, and said she would not move on until then.
A member said she has understood the committee as a go-between supporting SAP employees as well as taxpayers, and thanked the two members for raising the issue.
A member raised the loss of a grievance avenue for roughly 17-18 SAP employees, and the removal of seniority in layoffs.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to keep the current vacation carryover and payout language and not add a May 1 request date.

It accepted the termination-payout change, adding the word 'accrued' before 'unused vacation leave', and revised vacation approval and advance vacation wording; each vote passed with no dissent heard.
The meeting opened with members split over the committee's role, with concern that SAP changes on grievances and layoffs weaken employee protections; this was not resolved.
The paid holidays section, including Juneteenth, was tabled to the next meeting, with legal input requested.
The town manager said the old 10-month service requirement for vacation payout is not legal and accrued vacation must be paid at separation.

why_it_matters: These votes set how unused vacation is paid out when a town employee covered by the SAP leaves, a liability that lands on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The unresolved question of the committee's role bears on grievance rights and layoff seniority for roughly 17-18 SAP employees, which remain open.
watch_next: Next meeting: 5 o'clock on March 2 by Zoom, where the tabled paid holidays section returns.
